messages.author: b143fd3d839ce15c
messages.subject: Missing Data Linear Regression
parts:
So I'm trying to simulate a dataset where I do 
x <- runif(100, -100, 100)
y <- slope*x + intercept + rnorm(100, mean = 5, sd = 2)

And then I want to cut out like 10 of the x values and use STAN to find distributions for those x values.
I did this myself with my own Metropolis Hastings code, but I'd like to figure out the necessary model string and list that reads into stan so that stan can do it for me. 

Any help would be super appreciated 

here's what i've attempted so far:

model_string <- "
data {
  int<lower=0> N_obs;
  int<lower=0> N_mis;
  vector[N_obs] x;
  real y_obs[N_obs];
}
parameters {
  real alpha;
  real beta;
  real sigma;
  real y_mis[N_mis];
}
model {
  for (n in 1:N_obs)
    y_obs[n] ~ normal(alpha + beta * x, sigma);
  for (n in 1:N_mis)
    y_mis[n] ~ normal(alpha + beta * x, sigma);
}"

slope <- 5; intercept <- 5; x <- runif(100, -100, 100); sigma <- sqrt(6) #generate random uniform for w
y <- slope*x + intercept + rnorm(100, 0, sd = sigma) #regresson w using x
xy <- cbind(x, y) #bind the values 
truevalues <- xy[91:100 , ] #save the true values
y[91:100] <- NA #treat them as missing

mydata <- list(N_obs = 100, y = y[11:100], x=x) #turn data into list which is the only format stan will take
fit <- stan(model_code = model_string, data = mydata, iter = 2000, chains = 4)

edit: I think i'm using version 2.9.0-3

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Missing Data Linear Regression
parts:
Hi Kayla, 

First, I would highly recommend putting your Stan program in a separate file with a .stan extension rather than in a string. That way the line numbers in any error or warning messages will actually correspond to the line numbers of your Stan program. 

Regarding the contents of your Stan program, there are many ways you can write this model. Maybe the easiest way (given what you already have) is this (my changes in bold):

data {
  int<lower=0> N_obs;
  int<lower=0> N_mis;

vector[N_obs] x_obs;
  vector[N_mis] x_mis; // x-values for the obs with missing y

real y_obs[N_obs];
}
parameters {
  real alpha;
  real beta;

real<lower=0> sigma; // you need to have this <lower=0> here
  real y_mis[N_mis];
}
model {
  // vectorized (instead of loop) is cleaner and faster
  y_obs ~ normal(alpha + beta * x_obs, sigma);
  y_mis ~ normal(alpha + beta * x_mis, sigma);

  // optionally add priors for alpha, beta, sigma here (default is uniform)
}

With this Stan program, your list of data to pass into Stan from R would be something like this: 

list(N_obs = 90, N_mis = 10, y_obs = y[1:90], x_obs = x[1:90], x_mis = x[91:100])


Hope that helps, 

Jonah

> On Jul 28, 2016, at 1:16 PM, Kayla Montgomery <fallo...@gmail.com> wrote:

> So I'm trying to simulate a dataset where I do
> x <- runif(100, -100, 100)
> y <- slope*x + intercept + rnorm(100, mean = 5, sd = 2)

If you're trying to match, that mean = 5 will get absorbed
into the intercept.

In terms of fitting efficiency in Stan, it helps to standardize
so that the slope and intercept are on the unit scale (roughly
1 sd). Otherwise, Stan has to do the adaptation during warmup,
which should still work, but might require smaller initial step
sizes and longer warmup periods.

- Bob
